text:
Maria Chen: quick q — do we have an agreed story for queue durability vs slot granularity for continuous-batcher operator handoff? thinking about operator restarts and graceful eviction.
Dan Patel: not fully. two tradeoffs: durable queues (persist to SSD) -> slower enqueue/dequeue, more robust; ephemeral in-memory lanes -> faster but lose in-flight KV cache.
Ashley Gomez: if we persist, need versioned queue metadata + tombstones to avoid duplicate consumes. also ops: how to snapshot headroom without blocking admission.
Olivier: rough sketch: keep ephemeral in-memory primary, but snapshot tail every Xs and persist just lane offsets + batch boundary markers. on restart, replay tail only if missing ack; short-circuit if client-gen present.
Priya: can we co-design with admission controller? if admission tags requests with client-gen id we can dedupe on replay. client-gen would be per-tenant monotonically increasing id.
Maria Chen: :thumbsup: agree. also worried about long-tail restarts where head is large and replay costs spike (p50 vs p99 implications).
Dan Patel: maybe limit persistent replay size by truncating to last N requests per tenant and fail-fast older ones with 429 + degrade path. keeps recovery bounded.
Ashley Gomez: ops question: operator handoff — should we require a quorum handshake between old/new operator to transfer live slots? that needs an HA coordinator and makes rollout trickier.
SRE Bot: incident-bot: restart detected on cluster-3: operator-42 restarted 2025-06-12T14:02Z
Priya: handshake sketch: old operator writes TRANSFER intent to etcd with a short lease, new operator polls and claims if lease >= threshold. if old dies hard, new operator rebuilds from persisted snapshot + dedupe metadata.
Olivier: also need instrumentation: handoff-duration, replay-size, dedupe-rate, tail-replay-failures. sensible guardrails will let us alert before customer impact.
Maria Chen: action items: 1) prototype snapshot protocol (Olivier) 2) dedupe client-gen tagging (Priya) 3) ops runbook for large replays (Ashley) 4) perf estimate for SSD persist (Dan). i'll schedule a 30m follow-up.
Dan Patel: fyi here's a rough config proto i used for snapshot metadata: ```proto
message QueueSnapshot {
  string lane_id = 1;
  int64 head_offset = 2;
  repeated bytes batch_markers = 3;
}
```
Ashley Gomez: adding: consider soft-eviction where we move oldest batches to background spill to reduce replay time and keep operator warm.
Maria Chen: thanks all — i'll draft a short RFC fragment and post it in #eng-runtime for review.
